In the following figures, optical instruments are placed inside boxes (a) and (b). Which of the following options is correct for these?

(In box (a), two parallel rays enter horizontally and come out diverging — spreading apart from each other. In box (b), two parallel rays enter horizontally and come out converging to a single point on the right.)

options.label: A
options.text: In (b), the incident rays are converged after refraction, so lens is concave.

options.label: B
options.text: In (a), the incident rays are diverged after coming out of the box, so mirror is convex.

options.label: C
options.text: In (a), the incident rays are diverged after refractions, so lens is concave.

options.label: D
options.text: In (b), the incident rays are converged after coming out of the box, so mirror is convex.

stem:
Parallel rays from a distant tree are incident on a convex lens and form an image on the screen. The diagram correctly showing the image of the tree on the screen is:

A) Parallel rays pass through the convex lens and converge to a single point that lies exactly on the screen (the screen is placed at the focal plane, so a sharp point image of the distant tree falls on the screen).
B) None of these.
C) Parallel rays converge through the convex lens, but the screen is placed before the rays meet (in front of the focal point), so the rays have not yet converged at the screen and a blurred, larger arrow is drawn on it.
D) Parallel rays converge through the convex lens to a point, but the screen is placed beyond the focal point (after the rays have crossed), so the image is not sharp on the screen.

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram A — rays converge to a point exactly on the screen at the focal plane (sharp point image).

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram C — screen placed before the focal point, rays not yet converged.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram D — screen placed beyond the focal point, rays already crossed.

stem:
An object LMNO is placed in front of a concave mirror beyond the centre of curvature C as shown in figure. Which of the following is correct regarding the shape of the image?

(The figure shows a concave mirror on the right with its focus F and principal axis. On the axis, from far to near the mirror, the marked points are L, M, C, F. The object is a small two-dimensional shape LMNO: the segment LO is the taller, farther vertical edge at point L, and the segment MN is the shorter vertical edge at point M closer to the mirror. \(m_{LO}\) and \(m_{MN}\) denote the magnifications of the LO and MN portions of the object.)

Two plane mirrors A and B are aligned parallel to each other as shown in the figure. A light ray is incident at an angle 30° at a point just inside one end of A. The plane of incidence coincides with the plane of the figure. The maximum number of times the ray undergoes reflections (including the first one), before it emerges out, is

(The figure shows two horizontal parallel mirrors: A is the lower mirror and B is the upper mirror, separated by a vertical distance of 0.2 m. The mirrors have a horizontal length of \(2\sqrt{3}\,\text{m}\). The ray enters at the right end making an angle of 30° with the mirror surface and zig-zags to the left between the two mirrors.)

PQRS shows the walls of a room each measuring 8 m, such that wall PQ has a full length plane mirror. A camera is placed at point M, the mid point of wall SR. In order to take a clear image of the point R, the camera should be focused at.

(The figure shows a square room PQRS of side 8 m: P top-left, Q top-right, R bottom-right, S bottom-left. The top wall PQ is hatched, indicating a full-length plane mirror. M is marked at the mid-point of the bottom wall SR.)

A rectangular block of glass PQRS has a refractive index 1.6 and the critical angle for the glass air interface is 39°. A pin is placed midway on the face PQ. When observed from the face PS the pin shall

(The figure shows a square block of glass PQRS: P top-left, Q top-right, S bottom-left, R bottom-right. A pin, shown as a dot, is placed at the midpoint of the top face PQ. The observer looks in through the left vertical face PS.)

options.label: A
options.text: Appear to be near P always

options.label: C
options.text: Appear to be at the centre of PS

stem:
A converging set of rays, travelling from water (with refractive index \(\tfrac{4}{3}\) to air) is incident on a plane interface, the rays would have converged to a point 40 cm above the interface. However, due to refraction the rays will bend. At what distance above the interface will the rays actually converge?

(The figure shows a horizontal Air/Water interface with water below and air above. Two rays travelling upward inside the water are directed so that their backward extensions (dashed lines) would meet at a virtual point O located 40 cm above the interface in the air.)
